caption: Reference memory for extracting reusable poster language from a high-profile music award key visual. The transferable value is a method: identify the central metaphor, atmosphere, material texture, rhythm, typography hierarchy, content slots and replacement rules, then turn them into a clean GPT-image2 poster framework for new event themes.
positive_aesthetic_notes: design-language extraction separates reusable grammar from copyrighted official visuals
a central metaphor gives the poster emotional coherence before typography and decoration
prompt slots make event name, award name, edition, brand mark and title replaceable without losing hierarchy
negative_failure_notes: do not copy the official Golden Melody Awards visual, brand assets or exact poster composition
do not treat an extracted prompt framework as permission to clone a source campaign
avoid generic AI poster gloss without a clear metaphor and text hierarchy
text_accuracy_notes: Only user-supplied event names, award names, editions and titles should be exact. Official award names, brand marks and article copy must not be memorized as reusable text.
layout_notes: Prompt order: theme metaphor, central anchor, palette, texture, typography hierarchy, replaceable text slots, brand mark placeholder, series extension, forbidden copying rules.

caption: Metaphor-driven poster memory: an abstract event theme can be translated into a lifecycle-like visual anchor, restrained high-grade color, soft texture, quiet depth, and a typographic system that carries event identity without overwhelming the emotional image.
positive_aesthetic_notes: the best poster prompt begins with an abstract thesis rather than a list of visual effects
soft material texture can suggest music, resonance or growth without literal instruments
restraint makes the key visual feel ceremonial rather than noisy
negative_failure_notes: avoid stacking flowers, stages, spotlights, ribbons and particles without a governing metaphor
do not let decorative texture blur the event title or edition text
do not invent fake official logos or award seals
text_accuracy_notes: Large title and edition text must be provided or kept as clear placeholders. Small copy blocks should be schematic unless verified.
layout_notes: One dominant abstract anchor, one title block, one edition or event metadata block, optional logo placeholder, and a controlled blank field for breathing space.

caption: Prompt-slot framework memory for poster generation: define replaceable content variables before image style. Required slots include activity name, award name, English title, edition or year, brand mark placeholder, title hierarchy, supporting copy density and series variant rule.
positive_aesthetic_notes: content slots prevent text drift and reduce pseudo typography
a poster series becomes controllable when variables are named before visual effects
brand mark should remain a placeholder unless the user supplies authorized artwork
negative_failure_notes: do not generate official-looking award seals from memory
avoid pseudo-English or pseudo-Chinese text inside decorative typography
do not overload the prompt with style adjectives before locking content hierarchy
text_accuracy_notes: Use exact strings only from the current user brief. If no exact text is supplied, request placeholders such as EVENT NAME, AWARD TITLE, YEAR and LOGO MARK.
layout_notes: Use a stable template: header identity, central metaphor image, main title, sub-title, edition, metadata, footer sponsor zone and optional variant colorway.

caption: AI poster QA memory: after extracting a source style, check that the new poster has its own theme, own content, clean typography, no copied official marks, no source-image watermark, and no visual dependency on a copyrighted layout. The output should reuse structure-level reasoning, not source-specific assets.
positive_aesthetic_notes: source-safe training keeps inspiration as design logic instead of duplication
quality gates make AI posters more usable for real events
checking text before style prevents beautiful but unusable posters
negative_failure_notes: do not preserve source event names, article promotional text or official marks
avoid low-resolution web artifacts, watermarks and QR-like remnants
do not call a copied layout a template just because the text was replaced
text_accuracy_notes: Visible poster text must be exact, short, editable in later production and free of mojibake. Decorative microtext is a high-risk failure mode.
layout_notes: QA order: originality, theme fit, text accuracy, hierarchy, mark authorization, visual cleanliness, series consistency and export readiness.
